_comment: New-publication feeds for scripts/source_watch (see its README). Every URL here was opened and parsed on 2026-10-21. A topic keyword with a capital letter matches case-sensitively; an all-lowercase one ignores case. `match` names the item fields searched (default title + summary); `books` on a feed reports every new item of that feed for those books.

topics.name: Microsoft cloud identity and device management

feeds.name: CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog
feeds.source: CISA's KEV JSON feed (cisa.gov). Every entry's requiredAction cites the BOD, so only the name, product and description are matched.

feeds.name: NIST CSRC drafts open for comment
feeds.source: Linked from https://csrc.nist.gov/publications (Atom; a JSON twin exists at .../drafts-open-for-comment.json)

feeds.name: NIST CSRC publications (draft and final)
feeds.source: Linked from https://csrc.nist.gov/publications. CSRC publishes no feed of final publications; this spreadsheet lists every current FIPS, SP, IR, ITL Bulletin and CSWP, so a new row is a new publication or a new stage.

feeds.name: Federal Register (OMB, OPM, GSA, DHS/CISA, Commerce/NIST)
feeds.term: cybersecurity | "information security" | identity | authentication | cloud | FedRAMP | "zero trust" | "public key" | logging | "human capital"
feeds.source: https://www.federalregister.gov/developers/documentation/api/v1 (no key). CISA publishes under the homeland-security-department slug; the API has no separate CISA agency.

feeds.name: FedRAMP machine-readable rules (FedRAMP/rules commits)
feeds.source: https://github.com/FedRAMP/rules publishes fedramp-consolidated-rules.json, the structured FedRAMP Consolidated Rules for 2026. It has no releases yet, so commits are watched.

feeds.name: FedRAMP machine-readable rules (releases)
feeds.source: Releases of https://github.com/FedRAMP/rules (none as of 2026-10-21; watched in case they start).

feeds.name: CISA ScubaGear releases
feeds.source: Releases of https://github.com/cisagov/ScubaGear (CISA's M365 assessment tool; cisa.gov itself blocks automated readers, see README).

feeds.name: Microsoft CSV2SCIM sample (AzureAD/entra-id-inbound-provisioning commits)
feeds.source: Commits to Microsoft's CSV2SCIM sample, which examples/third_party/csv2scim pins at one commit (developer workbook Building the Attribute-Driven Migration, Chapter 01). A new commit means: review it, and update the snapshot only in a reviewed pull request.

feeds.name: Microsoft machine configuration package samples (Azure/azure-policy commits)
feeds.source: Commits to Microsoft's guest configuration package samples, which examples/third_party/guest-configuration-samples pins at one commit (developer workbook Building the Attribute-Driven Migration, Chapter 07). A new commit means: review it, and update the snapshot only in a reviewed pull request.

feeds.name: GuestConfiguration PowerShell module (Azure/GuestConfiguration commits)
feeds.source: Commits to the GuestConfiguration module's source. examples/machine-configuration pins version 4.12.0 in RequiredModules.psd1 (developer workbook Building the Attribute-Driven Migration, Chapter 07). A change here means: rerun tests/LearnBaseline.Tests.ps1 against the new version before moving the pin, in a reviewed pull request.

feeds.name: Learn's dynamic membership processing samples (MicrosoftDocs/entra-docs commits)
feeds.source: Commits to the Learn source pages that hold the five pause and resume samples, which examples/third_party/dynamic-membership-samples pins at one commit (developer workbook Building the Attribute-Driven Migration, Chapter 04). A new commit means: review it, rerun examples/dynamic-rules/tests/LearnSamples.Tests.ps1 on the new pages, and update the snapshot only in a reviewed pull request.

feeds.name: Learn's Logic App definition for Lifecycle Workflows custom task extensions (MicrosoftDocs/entra-docs commits)
feeds.source: Commits to the Learn source page that holds Microsoft's Logic App definition and authorization policies for custom task extensions, which examples/third_party/lifecycle-workflows-logic-app pins at one commit (developer workbook Building the Attribute-Driven Migration, Chapter 05). A new commit means: review it, rerun examples/lifecycle-extensions/tests/test_learn_sample.py on the new page, and update the snapshot only in a reviewed pull request.

feeds.name: Microsoft Intune settings catalog samples (microsoft/mggraph-intune-samples commits)
feeds.source: Commits to Microsoft's settings catalog export and import samples, which examples/third_party/mggraph-intune-samples pins at one commit (developer workbook Building the Attribute-Driven Migration, Chapter 06). A new commit means: review it, rerun examples/group-policy-as-code/tests/MicrosoftSamples.Tests.ps1 on the new scripts, and update the snapshot only in a reviewed pull request.
